## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is favoured: NSC 3/4 and all 10 nearest neighbours are Microtubule destabilizers with similarity 0.64–0.74, and frac_mitotic_like and tub_mean rise monotonically from 0.3 to 10 µM (rho=+1.00 each). The 10 µM well is the only actin-voting well (similarity 0.52, only 28 cells) and is plausibly a sparse high-dose outlier. The microscopist's stabilizer/Eg5 alternatives rest on bright rounded mitotic cells, but the report explicitly notes loss of filamentous microtubule network and inability to resolve spindle/bundle morphology; bright tubulin is confounded by rounding and does not specifically support stabilizers. Effects are large and consistent across four doses rather than a single weak well, so p=0.82 is reasonably calibrated.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ138** (no PubChem record shown)

Identity check: lookup failed: Neither PubChem nor ChEMBL knows 'AZ138'.

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule destabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Eg5 inhibitors**.

## Reflection

I correctly detected a potent dose-dependent antimitotic phenotype: frac_mitotic_like rose monotonically from 0.3 to 10 uM (rho=+1.00) with reduced density and very large tubulin/actin texture signals, and atlas matching was internally consistent with NSC 3/4 and 10/10 neighbours as Microtubule destabilizers. I also correctly flagged the single 10 uM Actin-disruptor vote as a sparse 28-cell low-similarity outlier rather than core biology, which rightly narrowed the field to mitotic arrest.

What misled me was that Eg5 inhibition produces the same low-resolution features: mitotic arrest and rounding-driven bright tubulin can mimic destabilizer texture. Eg5 inhibition induces mitotic arrest and cell death (PMID 19351824) via Eg5/KIF11-dependent arrest (PMID 28392145), while microtubule depolymerizers are also potent mitostatic agents (PMID 20110137). I overweighted quantitative similarity over the microscopist's early Eg5 candidate and explicit caution that loss of filamentous network could not resolve spindle/bundle morphology, and I treated rising tub_mean as destabilizer-specific when it is confounded by rounding.

The acquisition choice that locked in the error was spending all four wells on dose-trend strength at 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM without a discriminating morphology readout: no bipolar vs monopolar spindle scoring to test Eg5, despite monopolar formation being a known proliferation-suppressive arrest morphology (PMID 31679979). Next time I would keep the dose response but replace one well with high-resolution spindle counts plus a polymerization control.

What was right:
- Detected strong dose-dependent mitotic arrest with falling density across 0.3-10 uM, correctly placing AZ138 among antimitotics
- Recognized 10 uM well as sparse 28-cell low-similarity outlier rather than core phenotype
- Preserved microscopist observation of rounded mitotic-like cells with loss of filamentous network

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted increased tub_mean and extreme tub/act texture contrast as specific for microtubule destabilization when mitotic rounding concentrates tubulin in Eg5 arrest too
- Overweighted NSC 3/4 and 10/10 destabilizer neighbours and downweighted early Eg5 candidate without resolving spindle morphology
- Spent budget on four profiling doses for trend strength instead of acquiring bipolar vs monopolar spindle discrimination data

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution anti-tubulin plus DNA immunofluorescence to score bipolar vs monopolar spindles across 0.3-3 uM AZ138 versus Eg5-inhibitor and microtubule-destabilizer controls, paired with a cell-free tubulin polymerization assay to test direct depolymerizing activity.

## Citations

Citations verified: 4/4

- PMID [19351824](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19351824/): K858, a novel inhibitor of mitotic kinesin Eg5 and antitumor agent, induces cell death in cancer cells. *Cancer Res* (2009) — Eg5 inhibition induces mitotic arrest and cancer cell death, so dose-dependent mitotic accumulation does not specifically prove microtubule destabilization.
- PMID [28392145](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28392145/): HDAC Inhibitor-Induced Mitotic Arrest Is Mediated by Eg5/KIF11 Acetylation. *Cell Chem Biol* (2017) — Mitotic arrest can be mediated through Eg5/KIF11 regulation, explaining overlap with microtubule-agent profiles.
- PMID [20110137](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20110137/): Novel derivatives of 1,3,4-oxadiazoles are potent mitostatic agents featuring strong microtubule depolymerizing activity in the sea urchin embryo and cell culture assays. *Eur J Med Chem* (2010) — Microtubule depolymerizing agents are potent mitostatic agents, explaining why the atlas matched Eg5-induced arrest to destabilizers.
- PMID [31679979](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31679979/): Pyrenocine A induces monopolar spindle formation and suppresses proliferation of cancer cells. *Bioorg Med Chem* (2019) — Monopolar spindle formation suppresses proliferation, supporting spindle bipolarity as the needed discriminator.
